newsitem.title: FRANCE: Remains of WW1 soldiers found in France.
newsitem.headline: Remains of WW1 soldiers found in France.

text.p: Construction workers in northern France have unearthed the remains of 27 World War One soldiers believed to be British, the Commonwealth War Graves Commission said on Monday.
The mass grave, in the village of Monchy-le-Preux in the Pas-de-Calais department, was hastily dug in 1917, the commission said.
It said identity tags on three of the bodies should enable them to be rapidly identified.
The grave was found by workers digging foundations for a factory.
It contained bones, remnants of uniform, medals, buttons and insignia which were sent to the commission's offices to be examined.
